title: f83r P5: entry cues and complementary pauses in a whole performance instruction
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. A complete 62-group paragraph is provisionally read as instructions for a leader, followers and two accompaniment parts. Cue-owned entry and independently continuing accompaniment produce a dependency that a list of voices or arbitrary time shifts lacks. This adds a concrete target nomination to RAW364, not a new literal pes-code screen.

design.whole_content_draft: One singer starts with two accompaniment singers while the followers wait. Each following singer enters when the immediately preceding singer reaches the defined cue and sings the same melody. Everyone observes only the written pauses. One accompaniment part pauses at its end; the other pauses internally and restarts without an end pause. They repeat as needed. No finite stopping time or universal consonance law is asserted. This is a prose rule hypothesis, not a translation of either lyric or a word-by-word note score.
coupled_claims: Entry is a dependency on another singer’s motif position, not an arbitrary chosen delay.
The two accompaniment cycles continue while the number of active rota singers increases.
End versus internal pause belongs to a persistent part; the next sentence cannot swap it freely.
design.joint_consequence: An additional follower changes the active-voice count without resetting either accompaniment phase. Starting all singers together, or moving the lower part’s internal pause to its end, preserves a list of parts but changes the prescribed joint performance. The whole paragraph must distinguish these dependencies if this reading is right.
concrete_rivals: A catalogue of voices/parts has no cue-triggered entry requirement.
A single serial clock cannot represent the prescribed initial simultaneous leader and two pes starts.
Arbitrary independently delayed melodies need not enter at the previous singer’s owned cue.
lexical_and_syntax_debts: No written target cue, accompaniment owner, pitch, duration or number of singers is identified. The proposed six repeated word meanings are not enough to bind all rules.
The source admits selected two-, three- and four-rota-singer realizations plus two pes; four is not proved an absolute maximum.
No source-duration branch is selected. Native notation, ligature and prose/score disagreements remain as recorded.
The earlier source execution checked complete steady periods, not a separately audited initialization from zero.
The target’s many unknown words must carry the distinctions between same melody, previous singer, the two pause locations and repetition scope; they are not filled in individually here.
